items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: that boy would be at my house every day learning what I was learning him... And I learned him until he got to be a tough man.

ctx.x: I met him out there and I'd never known him here. I did hear him once in time but never talked to him before. I saw him in California.

Yeah. So he had a boy, used to work with him, bass violin, called Ranson. You might have heard of him. Yes I've heard of him. Ranson. He was doubling, he was playing bass fiddle and the horn. Well most of the time that boy would be at my house every day learning what I was learning him, you know what I mean? And I learned him until he got to be a tough man. And he worked out there on that sand boat where I was working at. He worked there a long time with Sidney Desbeam. And I worked in his place several times on…
